validity.researcher_notes: GEM records this row as Status=cancelled, ShelvedYear=2018, CancelledYear=2020 -- yet the sheet also already carries StartYear1=2019, which is the tell that something is off. Four independent, verified sources converge on the opposite conclusion -- this lateral was built and put into service, not cancelled: (1) The Oklahoman, Dec 14 2016 (reporting Enable's own announcement): Enable Midstream Partners LP signed a 20-year, 228,000 Dth/d gas supply contract with OG&E on the Enable Oklahoma Intrastate Transmission (EOIT) system, to build 77 miles of 20-inch pipe to OG&E's Muskogee plant, contract to start 2018. (2) Pipeline & Gas Journal 'Pipeline News' Ongoing Projects tracker, Oct 2018 issue (PDF, verified live): lists 'Muskogee Pipeline' under Enable Midstream Partners as 'Construction Underway' -- 68 miles, 20-inch, Oklahoma, Completion target 4Q 2018. (3) OGE Energy Corp SEC 10-K for FY2018 (filed 2019-02-21, verified live): 'OG&E has invested $50.5 million in the Muskogee natural gas conversion' as of Dec 31 2018, describing the project as actively 'converting.' (4) OGE Energy Corp SEC 10-K for FY2019 (filed 2020-02-27, verified live): states plainly 'OG&E converted two coal-fired generating units at the Muskogee Station to natural gas' and 'Muskogee Units 4 and 5 were placed into service in March 2019' -- and the FY2019 unit-by-unit generating-capability table lists Muskogee Units 4 and 5 as 'Steam-Turbine Gas' (changed from 'Steam-Turbine Coal' in the same table in the FY2018 10-K). The FY2020 10-K (filed 2021-02-25, verified live, read manually -- the automated substring check missed 'Steam-Turbine Gas' owing to HTML entity spacing around the table cells, hand-confirmed by reading the raw text) still shows Muskogee 4 and 5 running on gas with real 2020 capacity factors (14.8% and 14.0%), so the conversion was not later reversed. Three distinct origins (a newspaper covering Enable's announcement, an independent trade-press project tracker, and OG&E's own audited SEC disclosures) all point the same direction: the fuel-supply lateral this row represents was completed, which is *why* two 500 MW coal units could switch to gas -- a cancelled, never-built pipeline could not produce that outcome. No duplicate found among the 45-row roster (nearest is P2510 Canton, a different Enable/Energy Transfer Oklahoma project at Rose Valley, unrelated location). Classification (gas transmission lateral, not gathering) is correct as recorded. See status_reviews for the formal status-change record.

validity.researcher_notes: Two independent sources give two different lengths for the same lateral at two different project phases: The Oklahoman (Dec 2016, at contract announcement) says Enable 'will build 77 miles of 20-inch pipeline.' Pipeline & Gas Journal (Oct 2018, with construction underway) says 68 miles. 68 mi x 1.60934 = 109.4 km, which matches the sheet's recorded 109.00 km almost exactly, while 77 mi x 1.60934 = 123.9 km does not. This reads as a scope-refinement between an early public estimate and the actual/near-final construction figure, not an error in either source. Flagging so a future researcher does not 'correct' the sheet back toward the 77-mile figure without seeing this note.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: This is one of the rows the batch brief specifically flagged as a likely 'cancelled-but-actually-built' case, and the evidence bears that out cleanly. Timeline reconstructed from four/five documents across three independent origins: Dec 2016 (Oklahoman/Enable announcement of the 20-year, 228,000 Dth/d contract and planned 77-mi/20-in build); Oct 2018 (Pipeline & Gas Journal lists it as 'Construction Underway,' 68 mi, Completion 4Q 2018); OG&E's FY2018 10-K (filed Feb 2019) confirms $50.5M invested in the Muskogee conversion by year-end 2018, work ongoing; OG&E's FY2019 10-K (filed Feb 2020, the most direct evidence) states outright that 'Muskogee Units 4 and 5 were placed into service in March 2019' running on natural gas; OG&E's FY2020 10-K (filed Feb 2021, read manually since the automated substring check tripped on HTML entity spacing) still shows both units generating on gas with real 2020 capacity factors, so this was not a short-lived or reversed conversion. A pipeline the sheet calls cancelled cannot be the reason two 500 MW coal units successfully switched fuel -- the physical fact of the fuel switch is itself proof the lateral was built. Recommending Status -> operating, StartYear1/StartMonth1 = 2019/3 (matches what the sheet already had for StartYear1), and clearing ShelvedYear/CancelledYear/ShelvedCancelledType since no evidence of either event exists.
